Let $m_k$ be Stacy's money after leaving shop $k$, with $m_0 = d$. Each round she doubles her money at the lottery and then spends $1024$ at the next shop, so

$$m_k = 2m_{k-1} - 1024.$$

Subtracting the fixed point $1024$ from both sides gives $m_k - 1024 = 2(m_{k-1} - 1024)$, so

$$m_k - 1024 = 2^k (d - 1024).$$

She leaves the last of the 10 shops with nothing, so $m_{10} = 0$:

$$-1024 = 2^{10}(d - 1024) \implies d - 1024 = -1 \implies d = 1023.$$

Check: with $d = 1023$, $m_k = 1024 - 2^k$. This stays nonnegative, and before each shop she has $2m_{k-1} \ge 1024$ (the smallest is $2m_9 = 1024$), so every purchase is affordable. The equation determines $d$ uniquely, so the minimum is $1023$.

ANSWER: 1023
